one_line: Recent updates include the release of Mistral Large 4 and NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, alongside new hardware-efficient training systems and agent safety evaluations.

stories.title: Mistral Releases Weights for 1-Trillion-Parameter Mistral Large 4
stories.summary: Mistral has released the weights for Mistral Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model trained entirely on European infrastructure. The model matches leading open-weight coding performance while using 47% fewer tokens and blocking 96.6% of malicious cyber requests.
stories.why_it_matters: You can deploy a high-performing sovereign open-weight model that reduces token overhead for coding and offers robust cybersecurity defenses.
stories.editor_reason: Mistral releases weights for Mistral Large 4, an open frontier-class LLM release.

facts.claim: Mistral has officially released the weights for Mistral Large 4 (known as Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model.
facts.quote: Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model, now available with improved coding, cybersecurity, and reasoning efficiency.

facts.claim: The model has been developed and trained entirely on European infrastructure to support sovereign AI.
facts.quote: Trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage from inception to release, it gives organizations a trusted foundation for Sovereign AI

facts.claim: Mistral Large 4 achieved a 48% score on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, matching the leading open-weight model while utilizing 47% fewer tokens.
facts.quote: On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral Large 4 scores 48%, effectively tied with the leading open-weight model, GLM-5.3, while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average.

facts.claim: In cybersecurity evaluation, the model scores 51% on defensive tasks and blocks 96.6% of malicious cyber requests.
facts.quote: It retains strong performance on Cyber benchmarks, while achieving an average refusal rate of 96.6% on malicious cyber requests, the highest we measure among open models.

facts.claim: Vetted enterprise partners are receiving preview access to a specialized version of the model built for advanced security workflows.
facts.quote: We are also providing enterprise design partners such as Orange Cyberdefense, with preview access to a specialized variant of Mistral Large 4 optimized for advanced cybersecurity workflows

stories.title: Thrive Holdings Acquires ADT for $15.3 Billion Enterprise Value
stories.summary: Thrive Holdings, a holding company spinout from Thrive Capital that partners with OpenAI to revitalize companies with AI, has acquired ADT for $10 per share. ADT will now serve as the foundation for Thrive Holdings' smart home security business to develop new AI-powered products.
stories.why_it_matters: Thrive Holdings' acquisition of ADT for $15.3 billion enterprise value means the company will use ADT as the foundation for its smart home security business to release new AI-powered products.
stories.editor_reason: Thrive Holdings acquires ADT for $15.3B to integrate AI into physical security infrastructure.

facts.claim: Thrive Holdings acquired ADT for $10 per share, representing approximately $7.6 billion in equity.
facts.quote: Thrive Holdings has acquired physical security company ADT for $10 per share or about $7.6 billion in equity

facts.claim: The total enterprise value of the acquisition deal is $15.3 billion.
facts.quote: Beyond equity, the total enterprise value of the deal is $15.3 billion

facts.claim: Thrive Holdings is a holding company spinout from Thrive Capital that partners with OpenAI to revitalize companies with AI.
facts.quote: Thrive Holdings is the holding company spinout from Josh Kushner’s powerhouse VC firm Thrive Capital. It also counts OpenAI as its partner, as well as an investor.

facts.claim: As a result of the acquisition, ADT will become the foundation of Thrive Holdings' smart home security business and will release new AI-powered products.
facts.quote: ADT will form the foundation of Thrive Holdings’ smart home security business

first_issues.problem: Facts state Thrive Holdings 'partners with OpenAI', but do not state it is backed by OpenAI.

stories.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe for Multilingual Audio Processing
stories.summary: NVIDIA has released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a promptable open-weight model supporting transcription across 40 languages, translation, and speaker attribution. The model ranks first among open-weight options on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard for English with a 5.33% average word error rate.
stories.why_it_matters: You can leverage a top-tier open-weight model for accurate multilingual transcription and domain-specific audio fine-tuning.
stories.editor_reason: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, providing customizable multilingual speech-to-text models.

facts.claim: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open-weight, promptable model for multilingual transcription, translation, speaker attribution, and audio Q&A.
facts.quote: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, promptable model that turns recorded speech into useful text

facts.claim: The model supports 40 languages for transcription, translates 31 of them to or from English, and performs speaker attribution in 13 languages for up to eight speakers.
facts.quote: it transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 of them to or from English, and attributes speakers in 13. It handles recordings up to an hour long and labels up to eight speakers.

facts.claim: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ranks first among open-weight models on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard for English with a 5.33% average word error rate.
facts.quote: English: first among open-weight models at 5.33% average WER

facts.claim: Fine-tuning using Granary v2 data and NeMo Speech tools reduced the word error rate by 45.8% in a medical case study.
facts.quote: In a medical case study, fine-tuning cut word error rate (WER) on held-out speakers by 45.8% relative to the best prompt.

first_issues.problem: Facts say 'released', draft says 'launched', which slightly changes the scope/certainty regarding product availability.

stories.title: LRMoE Reduces Mixture-of-Experts Training Time on Memory-Constrained Nodes
stories.summary: Researchers introduced LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that recalibrates backward demand and balances workloads to mitigate GPU memory bottlenecks. Experiments show LRMoE reduces cumulative training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2-44.8% relative to SYMI.
stories.why_it_matters: You can train large Mixture-of-Experts models more efficiently on hardware with constrained memory by eliminating expert replication bottlenecks.
stories.editor_reason: Introduces LRMoE for demand-side load re-calibration, optimizing MoE training on memory-constrained hardware.

facts.claim: Uneven routing in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models creates bottlenecks, and additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory.
facts.quote: uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory.

facts.claim: The researchers present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload.
facts.quote: We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload.

facts.claim: During backpropagation, a load recalibration metric estimates token-expert pairs' contributions and selects pairs within specific quotas.
facts.quote: During backpropagation, a load recalibration metric estimates each token-expert pair's contribution to the expert update and selects pairs within these quotas.

facts.claim: LRMoE reduces cumulative MoE-layer training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2-44.8% relative to SYMI based on experiments with Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B.
facts.quote: Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B show that LRMoE reduces cumulative MoE-layer training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2-44.8% relative to SYMI.

stories.title: Double-Stratified Evaluation Protocol Improves Detection of Unsafe Tool Calls
stories.summary: Researchers proposed a double-stratification protocol separating injection exposure from behavioral commitment to evaluate latent monitors in tool-using agents. Retrained probe families using this approach can predict a model's unsafe tool calls up to two steps early.
stories.why_it_matters: You can implement more reliable internal monitoring to intercept indirect prompt injections and unsafe tool use in language agents.
stories.editor_reason: Presents rigorous double-stratified evaluation for latent monitors guarding tool-using agents against injection attacks.

facts.claim: Tool-using language agents are susceptible to indirect prompt injection, leading researchers to examine model internals to intercept unsafe actions.
facts.quote: Tool-using language agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, and a growing literature probes model internals to catch unsafe actions before they execute

facts.claim: The authors propose a double-stratification protocol that separates injection exposure from behavioral commitment.
facts.quote: propose a double-stratification protocol: separate injection exposure from behavioral commitment, in both the evaluation and the training population.

facts.claim: When retrained exclusively on exposed cases, probe families can predict a model's unsafe tool call up to two steps early.
facts.quote: Retrained on exposed cases only, the same probe families predict the model's own unsafe tool call up to two steps early

facts.claim: Specific models achieve high logistic AUROC scores when evaluated under the new approach, such as Mistral-7B reaching 0.896 and OLMo-2-7B reaching 0.912.
facts.quote: Mistral-7B reaches 0.896 and OLMo-2-7B 0.912
